records.name: Everywhere Project
records.summary: A Philadelphia harm reduction group that hands out food, clothing, and safer use supplies, teaches overdose reversal, and works to lower stigma against people who use drugs.
records.what_you_do: Help on the Wednesday and Saturday outreach, cook meals from home for the outreach, make harm reduction kits on Thursday evenings, or drop off gently used clothing. The volunteer survey is now closed, so questions go through the contact form.

schedule.text: Love Park outreach on Wednesday evenings, Kensington outreach on Saturday afternoons, and kit making on Thursday evenings.

locations.label: Love Park outreach site
locations.address: 1501 JFK Blvd, Center City, Philadelphia PA

locations.label: Kensington outreach site
locations.address: Ruth St and Clearfield St, Kensington, Philadelphia PA

cost.text: The outreach services are described as no-barrier, and no fee is listed for them or for donating clothing.

first_step.how: Send a question through the contact form at everywhereproject.org, under Questions about volunteering, asking about the next Wednesday or Saturday outreach shift.
first_step.basis: The public volunteer survey is closed, and the site does not describe volunteer training, screening, or a first shift. Questions go through a contact form, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Tier 1 sent people to the volunteer survey, but that form now reads as closed, so the first step is replaced. The donate page calendar lists Love Park outreach at 6:45 pm on Wednesdays and Kensington at 12 pm on Saturdays; the services page gives 7 to 9 pm and 1 to 4 pm. The calendar times may be volunteer arrival times, so they are not published. Last sign of life is the Thanksgiving Eve 2025 event named on the services page; the month 2025-11 comes from the holiday itself. The site has no first-visit detail, so what_to_expect and tips are left out. The cooking form asks volunteers to cook at home and bring food to a central site for one or both outreach days; food is provided and no certification is asked for. No partner organizations are named on the pages read.

records.name: Fair Amount Food Forest
records.summary: A community food forest in Fairmount Park where neighbors plant, tend, and harvest together, with plant walks, cooking and preserving workshops, and a farmers market.
records.what_you_do: Join a planting or tending session, or come to a free workshop on herbs, preserving, pruning, or fruit trees. Vendors can apply to sell at the farmers market.

schedule.text: A first Saturday work party from 10 am to 3 pm (February through December), Tuesday guided harvests from noon to 7 pm (mid-March through November), Thursday sessions from 4 to 7 pm (April through November), and a third Saturday plant walk and herbal workshop in the afternoon (March through November).

cost.text: Most workshops and plant walks are free, usually with a free RSVP. The wine making classes are for ages 21 and up.

access.notes: The food forest is all outdoors and has no indoor bathroom. A portable toilet is on site from April through November, and it is open only during programs.

first_step.how: Come to the first Saturday work party at 10 am, or walk in to a workshop; the events page says walk-ins are always welcome, though workshop supplies are limited to 25 people.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says newcomers can join and that all ages and experience levels are welcome to the first Saturday program, and the events page says walk-ins are always welcome. No beginner day or orientation is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Work parties run on the first Saturday of the month from 10 am to 3 pm and include a guided harvest. Volunteers are asked to dress for the weather and bring their own water bottle. Workshop supplies are limited, with priority for people who registered in advance, so arriving early helps.
first_visit_tips: Dress for the weather and wear sturdy footwear
Bring your own water bottle
Arrive by 10 am for the first Saturday work party
Do not pick plants or fruit on your own outside a staffed program

records.notes: The events page lists dates by weekday and month without a year. The 2026 year on last_sign_of_life is matched from the weekdays (Saturday, October 10 falls on a Saturday in 2026), so it rests on that match. The third Saturday walk ends at 5 pm on the events page and at 5:30 pm on the volunteer page, so the schedule says afternoon. The wine making classes are for ages 21 and up, and that is kept out of the schedule because it is one of several series. Parking and transit are not stated. Partner named on the events page: Fairmount Park Conservancy (leads_only).

records.name: Familiar Hearts Animal Society
records.summary: A small rescue in Mt. Airy that cares for animals until they find homes, using foster families, adoption, and a pet pantry program.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the volunteer application, foster animals in your home through the foster application, or adopt through the adoption application. Donations from the wish lists are welcome.

schedule.text: No set weekly schedule is listed. Volunteer and foster sign-ups happen through the website forms, and adoption visits are arranged through foster caregivers.

locations.label: Registered address in Mt. Airy (no public shelter to visit)

cost.text: Adoption fees: dogs $475, puppies up to 12 months $600, cats $150 or $225 for a pair, kittens up to 12 months $200 or $350 for a pair. Foster homes receive supplies and veterinary care. The page does not list volunteer costs.

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer Application on the volunteer page, or the Foster Application if you can take an animal into your home.
first_step.basis: Volunteering, fostering, and adopting each start with an application form, and adopters meet animals only after approval. The site does not say whether anyone can visit before applying.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists volunteer roles such as dog walking, cat socialization, animal transport, photography, writing pet bios, fundraising events, and grant research. It does not say how long a shift runs or whether training is given. There is no shelter to walk into, because the group works through foster homes.
first_visit_tips: Read the foster guide on preparing for a foster dog before you apply to foster
Expect the adoption steps to start with an application and reference checks
Check your email and spam folder often after you apply, since the adoption steps run by email

records.notes: The address 6915 Greene St comes from the tier 1 record. The volunteer and foster pages say the group is foster based with no central shelter, and the footer lists no address, so the address is labeled as a registered address and should be checked before publishing. The events page did not load on this pass (the calendar says it is best viewed on a large screen), so no event dates are listed. Newcomer friendliness moved from 3 to 2 because every route starts with an application. Adoption fees come from the adoption process page. The foster page says the foster network reaches within about two hours of headquarters, which is not published here.

records.name: Fast Break Philly
records.summary: A sports group for girls and gender-expansive youth in Philadelphia. Its fall volleyball clinics run for grades 3 to 8 and its Sunday ultimate frisbee clinics for grades 4 to 9. Clinics are paid by the session, with a lower community rate.
records.what_you_do: Players sign up online for volleyball clinics at Greene Street Friends School or ultimate clinics at Edgely Ultimate Fields. Each session is paid separately, and the group keeps an email list for news.

schedule.text: Fall clinics on Sundays. Volleyball runs in the morning: grades 3 to 6 from 10 to 11:30 am, grades 7 and 8 from 11:30 am to 1 pm, and sixth graders may pick either session. Ultimate runs from 3 to 4:30 pm on Sundays.

cost.text: Volleyball is $25 per session or $100 for all five. Ultimate is $10 per session. A lower community rate applies: $15 per volleyball session or $60 for all five, and $6 per ultimate session, entered with a code at checkout.

first_step.how: For ultimate, complete the online registration form on the Ultimate Frisbee clinic page for the next Sunday session. Volleyball is full, so email info@fastbreakphilly.com to join its waitlist.
first_step.basis: Both clinic pages say all experience levels are welcome and give a public registration form. Volleyball has reached its cap and is waitlist only, so its way in is the waitlist.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe tryouts or a first session in detail. The ultimate clinics teach the fundamentals of the game, skill building, and team play, with a focus on confidence. The earlier volleyball session for each grade band focuses on fundamentals, and the later one adds more game play.
first_visit_tips: Pick the session that matches the player's grade, since volleyball is split by grade
Sixth graders may choose either volleyball session
Have the school, grade, level of play, and caregiver contact details ready for the form
Join the email list to hear about schedule changes

records.notes: Volleyball registration page says the program has reached its participant limit and is waitlist only. The ultimate page lists its Sunday dates as October 4, November 1, and December 13, while the homepage listed December 6; the October 4 session has already passed. The volleyball page labels the older group with a typo (6th7th/8th), so the grade split follows tier 1 and the 6th grade choice is noted separately. Eligibility on both pages is girls, non-binary, and gender-expansive youth; grades are not converted to ages. No volleyball tag exists in the vocabulary, so youth_coaching was chosen as the closest fit. The community rate code is on the registration page and is deliberately not reproduced. The ultimate page names Philadelphia Area Disc Alliance as a partner, and the homepage says the group is powered by Girls Belong Foundation (both in leads_only). The homepage mentions a 2026 season label but no dated post, so last sign of life is left out. No EIN was found on the pages read, so it is left out.

records.name: The Fathering Circle
records.summary: A peer support group for men who are raising a young person. Men 17 and older meet every Monday evening to talk with other men in the same position.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Monday evening circle at the Philip E. Lindy House and talk with other men who are raising a young person. Anyone who identifies as a male caregiver or parent can join, whether or not they are a biological father.

schedule.text: Peer support circle every Monday, 6 to 7:30 pm.

locations.label: Philip E. Lindy House (Drexel Dornsife Center)

first_step.how: Register for a Monday circle through its Eventbrite listing, or email info@thefatheringcircle.com to ask about joining before you come.
first_step.basis: The 2024 join post names Eventbrite, email, and phone as ways in, but the group's own contact page is a form with no join steps, and the post does not say whether a first visit is drop in. Attendance is limited to men 17 and older raising a young person.
first_step.what_to_expect: The circle is a peer support group where men talk with each other about raising a young person. The group does not describe its session format or activities on its pages.
first_visit_tips: Ask first whether a new man can drop in or must register
If email does not get a reply, call 215-487-5918, the number in the 2024 join post
Check the Facebook group for news about upcoming circles

records.notes: The email and phone number come only from the October 2024 join post; the contact page shows just a form and publishes no email or phone. Confirm them before publishing. The June 7, 2026 Wilma Theater post is the newest dated evidence. Cost is not stated on any page read; the Eventbrite listing is titled tickets but Eventbrite is a lead site and was not read. Newcomer friendliness stays at 2 because the join route is a sign-up and the first-visit format is unclear. Partner named in the June 2026 post: Wilma Theater (leads_only).

records.name: Fayton Foundation
records.summary: A Northwest Philadelphia group that runs a weekly food program for neighbors and seniors, a Sunday prayer gathering, a spring neighborhood cleanup, and school coaching and scholarships.
records.what_you_do: Get a meal or food box on Tuesdays, join the Sunday Prayer Cafe, or come out for the spring cleanup of green spaces.

schedule.text: Food program every Tuesday, 11 am to 1 pm. Prayer Cafe every Sunday at 9:30 am.

locations.label: Prayer Cafe at Holsey Temple Church

cost.text: The site does not say whether any program costs money. It has a donate button and notes that donations are tax deductible in the United States.

first_step.how: Come to the Tuesday food program at 5305-15 Germantown Ave between 11 am and 1 pm, or walk in to the Sunday Prayer Cafe at 9:30 am at 5305-11 Germantown Ave.
first_step.basis: The Prayer Cafe is a drop-in gathering where all are invited, and the food program runs set Tuesday hours. The site does not say whether the food program needs registration, ID, or meets any eligibility rule.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Prayer Cafe is a short drop-in gathering for a moment of spiritual uplift. The Tuesday food program serves meals and offers emergency food, along with clothing and health and social support resources, with volunteers serving alongside students from Germantown Friends School. The site does not say how long a visit takes or whether anyone has to register.
first_visit_tips: Arrive during the 11 am to 1 pm window on Tuesdays
Ask by email before your first visit, since the site leaves out registration and ID details
Expect the Prayer Cafe to be a short drop-in at 9:30 am on Sundays

records.notes: The Sunday Prayer Cafe (9:30 am, Holsey Temple Church, drop-in, all invited) was confirmed from a search result that quotes the group's own site; one homepage read and the our-work page did not show it, so recheck before publishing. The spring cleanup appears in one homepage read and in tier 1 but not on the other pages checked, so it has no date and no details here; verify it before visiting. The contact page shows FaytonFoundation@gmail.com while the footer shows support@faytonfoundation.org, which opens the Gmail address; the contact page address is used. The Community Impact 2025 report lists a December holiday celebration, which is the source for last sign of life (2025-12, the year is from the report title). The scholarship and second grade coaching program pages give no application or eligibility details. Partner named on the food program page: Germantown Friends School (leads_only). The Facebook and Instagram pages were not read.

records.name: Feliz Filadelfia
records.summary: A community group in Olney that uses sports to help kids grow. It runs seasonal baseball, softball, soccer, flag football, and basketball teams, plus a garden club and community center activities.
records.what_you_do: Families register kids for seasonal teams in several sports, or take part in the garden club and community center activities. Each season has its own registration page, and questions go to the group by email.

schedule.text: Soccer practices on Mondays and Wednesdays, 4:45 to 6 pm. Garden club on Mondays and Wednesdays, 4:15 to 5 pm. Baseball, basketball, and flag football run in their own seasons, each with its own sign-up page.

cost.text: No fee is listed on the registration pages read. Ask by email before you sign up.

first_step.how: Fill in the online soccer registration form, or sign up in person at Hammond Fields. The fall baseball sign-up closed August 23, 2026, so email info@felizfiladelfia.org about other seasons.
first_step.basis: Sign-up pages are public, soccer takes online or in-person registration, and the group lists an email contact. The baseball window has closed for the season, and the site describes no volunteer or coaching route.
first_step.what_to_expect: Soccer practices meet on Mondays and Wednesdays from 4:45 to 6 pm at Hammond Fields. The registration form asks for the child's details, school, medical concerns, pickup people, and a waiver, and the page does not describe tryouts or the first practice.
first_visit_tips: Have the child's birth date, school, and grade ready for the form
Be ready to list who can pick the child up
Accept the waiver and photo release, which the form requires
Ask by email which team or age group your child fits

records.notes: Tier 1 had last sign of life 2026-10 with no source; the baseball registration page gives a written date (registration closing August 23, 2026), so that date is used instead. The soccer page is headed Starting April 1st with no year, and a news item says the fall season kicked off September 21 with no year, so no season dates are published. The garden club starts April 2 (no year written). The flag football page is labeled 2025 and basketball 25-26, so those sign-up pages may be out of date. Ages: soccer is for boys and girls ages 6 to 14, and the baseball form heading says ages 10 to 19; neither is set as a min or max age because the programs differ. The soccer waiver names Street Soccer USA (leads_only). No volunteer route is described; the contact page lists email as the only way to reach the group.
